description.value: A multimodal study examined the relationship between reward-sensitive P300 amplitudes and prefrontal gray matter volume in healthy controls and individuals with cocaine use disorders, and compared regional gray matter volume between groups.

spans.text: Our objective in this study was therefore to evaluate whether the neural mechanisms indexed by the P300, as modulated by the preparation of a reward-contingent response, were associated with PFC gray matter (GM) volume in a healthy participant group.

description.value: An observational, cross-sectional comparison of healthy controls and individuals with cocaine use disorders; structural MRI and EEG recordings were obtained within one week of one another.

spans.text: Structural scans were obtained from all participants within 1 week (1.79 ± 2.88 days) of completing the psycho-physiological recordings and clinical interviews
